label: copy phase, later outputs, biased to inputs o/l/i/p/d/h/2/3
explanation: Fires only in the copy phase (t > L), never during the original tokens or on <DEL>. It never fires on the first copy output (recall_idx 0) and rarely on recall_idx 1 (about 3.6% of mass, nearly all in L=3). It never fires when the input token appears for the first time in the sequence. Inside the copy phase it is sparse (about 12% of copy steps) and depends on the token. It favours the inputs o, l, 2, i, 3, p, d, h (rate 2-3x baseline) and outputting c. It also favours the last two outputs (to_go <= 1, 59% of mass) and L=3 (rate 0.28; the top activations are all L=3 at the final output). Magnitudes are tiny (max 0.002) and largest for L=3 final outputs. Phase alone gives recall 1.0 at precision 0.12. The best predicate (copy phase, recall_idx >= 2, input token in that set) reaches dev F1 0.40 and mass recall 0.61, so much of the step-by-step selectivity is not captured by simple variables.
